what_this_measures: Zero-boat cost of the world-entity descent. Both executables link the SAME frozen application objects; only the control's temporary painters_bucket.u.c replaces the two `if( scenery_is_world_entity(element) )` branches with `if( 0 )`. Every scene here is boat-free, so any delta is the cost of evaluating that predicate per scenery element, not of drawing a vessel. It is a compiled-out causal control, not a comparison against an older client.

provenance.benchmark_executables_are_NOT_the_shared: The frozen pair could not be built from the shared objdir. src/build_opt_es/torirs_server_world.o had been deleted by tools/objverify.py because another session saved src/torirsserver/torirs_server_world.c at 08:37:39, AFTER root's 08:08 shared build; and `make` in the shared objdir was refused by this session's permission layer. The pair was therefore linked against a PRIVATE full build of the current sources (PLATFORM_OBJ_BASE=build_perf -> src/build_perf_opt_es, 436 objects, built 08:54), selected by MAKEFLAGS='PLATFORM_OBJ_BASE=build_perf' with no edit to tools/sailing_render_acceptance.py. Nothing in src/build*, src/torirs or src/build_opt/torirsserver was written; both shared hashes were re-verified unchanged afterwards and the newest file in src/build_opt_es is still 08:10.

pair.source_diff_verified_by_hand: diff of the two temporary painters_bucket.u.c files is exactly 2 lines (the two branch conditions); painters.c is byte-identical between halves

comparisons.visual_inspection: Lumbridge from directly overhead: castle courtyard walls, the stone fountain, the wooden bridge over the Lum, two hedgerows, blue-awning stalls along the west wall, a moored canoe on the river at top-left, river water top-right.

Varrock square from overhead: the cruciform stone fountain with four blue water quadrants, striped market-stall canopies, the roofed building top-left, tree canopies right, two banners on the north wall.

Grand Exchange interior floor filling the frame, dark cobble with per-tile pebble relief and a wall edge at top-left. A low-information frame: real geometry, but almost all of the scene's 4,091 painter commands are outside or occluded by this camera.
Grand Exchange from a low camera: the multi-storey ring wall on the horizon, the enclosing balustrade with lamp posts, trees, grass, a dirt path with a bench at right.
Orbiting camera over the Grand Exchange floor: the dark cobble apron, its cream border kerb and the black balustrade running diagonally, grey flagstone paving in the lower band.
Moving camera over Varrock: a large grey tiled roof filling the lower half, the cobbled street with scattered stones, a blue tent canopy, wooden fences, trees, buildings with green-shuttered windows.
Falador from overhead: a road crossroads, four buildings with red tiled roofs and white stone walls, blue-glazed windows, grass verges, stone steps.
Lumbridge swamp: green swamp water, grey rocky islands, dead branches, teal reed/plant sprites, yellow-green shallows at the edges.
Ground-level camera on the Grand Exchange floor: dark cobble receding to a distant lit wall band at the top, pale flagstones across the bottom edge. Deliberately a ground-plane scene.

Varrock square at ground level and the densest frame in the suite: the fountain with its two statues and blue water, the blue-and-white striped tent, market stalls, Varrock buildings with green doors, trees, a spinning wheel at left.

Falador street at ground level: the statue on its plinth in mid-frame, white stone buildings both sides with red roofs and blue windows, grass verges, the castle gate arch and two spired posts at the end of the street.

Lumbridge castle courtyard at ground level: the battlemented curtain wall on three sides, the fountain, a tree, clipped hedges, stone steps, blue wall banners, arrow slits, a wooden bench, a bluebell plant, and the boulder at the near edge.

follow_ups_for_scenes_beyond_noise.note: Both scenes were re-measured ALONE with --repeat 5 --reuse-build against the same frozen executables (hashes re-verified before each run). The unfavourable 3-repeat suite numbers are preserved above and repeated here.

grand-exchange-orbit.verdict: Resolved. +8.23% at 3 repeats was a single outlier sailing window (2.088 ms); at 5 repeats the scene is +0.18% render and -1.99% paint.

alone_5_repeats_run_A.note: This run did NOT come back neutral: +1.99% render, sailing above control in 4 of 5 windows. Not significant at 0.05, so a second independent run was taken rather than accepting either sign.

falador-ground.verdict: Not reproducible, therefore treated as noise, but stated with its numbers rather than dropped: +4.53% (3 repeats) -> +1.99% (5 repeats, p=0.119) -> +0.32% (independent 5 repeats, p=1.0). The largest honest upper bound this scene supports is about 0.07 ms on a 3.47 ms render stage.

verdict.pixels_and_work: Neutral and proven: 12/12 boat-free scenes render byte-identical images and identical painter_commands / r_cmds_model / scene_elements counts with the descent enabled.
verdict.cost: Neutral within measurement error. Across the 12 scenes the render p50 delta is a median of +0.32% and a mean of +1.09%, and the mean is pulled up entirely by the two scenes that did not reproduce on repetition; with grand-exchange-orbit and falador-ground replaced by their 5-repeat re-measurements the mean falls to about +0.1%. Seven of twelve scenes are negative on paint (median paint delta -1.97%), which is itself evidence that the residual is run-to-run variation and not a real cost. In absolute terms the largest reproducible per-scene render difference is under 0.07 ms on stages of 0.9-3.6 ms.
verdict.claim: The zero-boat path is neutral: with no vessel in the scene the world-entity descent changes no pixel, no work count, and no measurable time.
